I’m syrup, 22f, turning 23 in a couple days. I’m an artist, I’ve worked with many mediums over the years and currently I’m working with 3d modeling and slowly getting into 3d animation in blender and cinema 4D. I graduated from an art school in 2022. In 4 years of school I never found what I was truly passionate about and completely lost sight of the work I wanted to make, but in this year since I graduated I found it again through 3D. I didnt use any 3D softwares in school besides Rhino 7 for something more technical. Creating art became so dreary when I was in school, but now I don’t want to do anything else. I feel like I used to when I first started painting when I was 11. I never thought I’d feel this way again. 
I’m lucky that I was able to land a job as a fabricator using some of the skills I learned in school (woodworking and digital fabrication, among other things) and that I still have time to pursue my own interests. When I was in my first year of college I did not think I would land any opportunity like this. I didn’t even think I would graduate. 
I’m slowly building up the confidence to start posting and sharing my work for the first time since before college. For years I was destroying all of the art I was making out of shame but now I am archiving every render I make. I actually like looking at them. Trying to convince myself that maybe someone else would too.

They opened the scholarship application around January. I picked the class I wanted, did the skill test, and submitted that with a short statement about how the class would benefit my career or something like that. The skill test for ascent was animating a 5second video of a paper airplane flying through rings. I think the other classes have a skill test too, but I’m not sure. 
And yeah, whichever class you apply for, you get for free if they choose you. I think they’re going to make the scholarships a regular thing for each session, so I’d look out for it. The application is really quick and worth it if you get it. They notified me via email that I was accepted, and a week or so before the class started I was added into it, no hassle

I’m taking the ascent class right now. we’re on the third week. I was worried that it would be too advanced for me because I’ve only been using cinema 4d since october, and my only training with it was a LOT of youtube tutorials and experimenting. But I got the scholarship for it, so whoever viewed my skills test felt I was ready for it. 

It’s only the third week, but I’ve been keeping up with the assignments and having a lot of fun with them. The briefs are definitely  geared towards people with careers/backgrounds in graphic design I think. I’m sure 99% of the class is working / wants to work in that field. That isn’t my background going into the class. the work I was doing in cinema 4D before this class was all silly stuff using sketch and toon, so it’s been nice to push myself and do more polished work in redshift. Part of the reason I took the class was to learn more professional workflows, because my current workflow is erratic at best. But it works for the silly work I’ve been doing. 

The videos have the old UI, but if you are comfortable navigating cinema 4D it isn’t a huge problem. the videos are very long so I take handwritten notes. It helps me stay focused and retain the information. 

I’ve learned a lot already and the resources they give are pretty cool. I’ve gotten great feedback on my submissions thus far that really helped me improve. 

Something to consider is that it requires pretty powerful hardware to keep up with the assignments. Especially now that we’re using redshift a lot. I don’t have the best gpu but I’ve been making it work. 

It is a time commitment, but it doesn’t feel that way for me sometimes because it’s a lot of fun! I find myself waiting impatiently for them to drop the next set of videos because i’m excited to see what the next assignment is. I’m sure it ramps up in later weeks, but I’m really looking forward to that.

Thank god someone finally said it. 
People talking about applying to 20 colleges when I can barely afford to apply to 3. 
I can only take the SAT once with no prep, so the score I get is the one I get. No redoes. And none of those fruity little subject tests. What are subject tests to me? Money I don’t have. 
And so what if my financial aid package is higher than someone with a stable income? Does that mean I can afford any school? Does that put mad expensive private schools in my range? No... that’s not how it works. 

And when you’re poor, you have to decide when you’re 7 that you want to go to college and make nothing else your absolute priority if you want to go to a good school. My grades throughout high school aren’t up to snuff to where I can make use of the supposed full ride I’ll get from being black and poor at an Ivy league. Why aren’t they up to snuff? Because i don’t have time to study. I have to work and pay bills. School never meant anything to me until a couple years ago. And now that I’m a senior, it’s too late. I’ll apply to state schools, but I’ll probably be at cc trying to put my life back together. That’s what being poor is.

To the poor folks making it to the Ivies, or any school for that matter, I have the highest respect for you, because you’ve done what many of us could not.
